title: Grade 4 Science — Mon, May 25
description: Rocks & Minerals — Day 1 of 5: Types of rocks
subject: science

questions.question: How many main types of rocks are there?
questions.explanation: There are 3 types of rocks: Igneous, Sedimentary, and Metamorphic.

questions.question: Igneous rocks are formed by:
questions.explanation: Igneous = 'fire' (Latin). Formed when magma (underground) or lava (above ground) cools and solidifies.

questions.question: Which is an example of an igneous rock?
questions.explanation: Granite is a common igneous rock. Basalt is another. Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary; marble is metamorphic.

questions.question: Sedimentary rocks are formed by:
options: Layers of sand, mud, shells pressing together over millions of years
questions.explanation: Sedimentary = 'layers'. Tiny pieces (sediments) settle, get buried, pressed, and cemented into rock.

questions.question: Which is a sedimentary rock?
questions.explanation: Sandstone is sedimentary (sand grains cemented together). Limestone and shale are also sedimentary.

questions.question: Metamorphic rocks are formed when:
options: Rock changes form due to extreme heat and pressure deep underground
questions.explanation: Metamorphic = 'changed form'. Existing rock transforms under high heat and pressure — without melting.

questions.question: Which is a metamorphic rock?
questions.explanation: Marble is metamorphic (limestone changed by heat+pressure). Slate is another metamorphic rock.

questions.question: Fossils are most commonly found in which type of rock?
questions.explanation: Fossils form in sedimentary rock because organisms get buried in sediment layers that slowly harden.

questions.question: Which type of rock comes directly from a volcano?
questions.explanation: Lava from volcanoes cools into igneous rock (e.g., basalt). Volcanoes produce igneous rock.

questions.question: Limestone (sedimentary) + heat + pressure = ?
questions.explanation: Heat and pressure change limestone into marble. This is how metamorphic rock forms from sedimentary rock.

questions.question: How do we identify igneous rock?
options: It looks crystalline or glassy, no layers, very hard
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks are typically crystalline (granite) or glassy (obsidian), very hard, no layers, no fossils.

questions.question: Which characteristic helps identify sedimentary rocks?
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks show visible layers (strata) — each layer represents different time periods of deposition.

questions.question: Coal is an example of:
questions.explanation: Coal forms from compressed plant matter over millions of years — it is a sedimentary rock.

questions.question: Which type of rock would you most likely see at the top of a mountain that was once a seabed?
questions.explanation: Ancient seabeds are sedimentary. Many mountain tops have sedimentary rocks formed when they were underwater.

questions.question: Summary: match rock type to formation process
options: All three form the same way
questions.explanation: Igneous → from magma/lava. Sedimentary → compressed sediment layers. Metamorphic → existing rock changed by heat+pressure.
